topic: Fundamentals of Linear Algebra: From Spans to Bases

sections.title: Prerequisite Refresh: Vectors as Arrows
lecture_lines: Vectors represent both magnitude and direction.
Add two vectors: tip to tail.
Scale vectors: stretching or shrinking length.
Vectors are building blocks of linear space.
animations: Create vector v from origin (0,0) to point (2,1) using #FFFF00.
Show arrow label 'v' beside the vector in #FFFFFF.
Animate vector v scaling by 1.5 to demonstrate scalar multiplication.
Add vector u=(1,2) to v to show vector addition (head-to-tail).
Final display of vector sum result as a new color #00FF00.

sections.title: Linear Combinations and Span
lecture_lines: The Span is the reach of all combinations.
Robot movements combine to cover the floor.
Span reveals all reachable space points.
animations: Animate two vectors u and v starting from the origin in #FF00FF and #00FFFF, represented by a to indicate the starting point.
Show grid lines extending across the 2D plane to indicate reachable space.
Demonstrate linear combination c1*u + c2*v by tracing paths on the grid.
Flash the entire plane area to emphasize 'Span' of the set {u, v}.
Highlight the final spanned 2D area in a soft color #333333, with the marking the boundary of the spanned region.

sections.title: Linear Dependence: The Redundancy Rule
lecture_lines: Dependent vectors share same line or plane.
Redundant vectors add no new directions.
animations: Display three vectors u, v, w in #FF6666, #66FF66, #6666FF, using a to measure their lengths.
Rotate w to align exactly with the sum of u and v.
Display 'Dependent' text in #FF0000 near the collinear vectors, highlighting the relationship with a.

sections.title: Bases: The Minimalist Toolkit
lecture_lines: Basis is the minimal spanning set.
Basis vectors must be linearly independent.
Unit vectors (1,0) and (0,1) form a basis.
animations: Display standard unit vectors i=(1,0) and j=(0,1) in #FFFF00.
Show a grid formed by i and j covering the plane.
Display 'Basis' text in #00FF00 as the minimal toolkit.

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
lecture_lines: Span: the reach of your vectors.
Independence: the efficiency of your set.
Basis: the perfect, minimal tool set.
animations: Fade in labels for 'Span', 'Independence', and 'Basis' and introduce the to represent direction.
Use arrows to connect these labels into a cycle diagram.
Highlight the text 'Efficiency' in #FFFF00 and overlay the to conclude.
